name: Communist Party of India
description: The Communist Party of India (CPI) is one of India's oldest political parties. Established in 1925, it advocates democratic socialism, workers' rights, agrarian reforms, secularism and social justice. It has played an important role in labour movements, student politics and parliamentary democracy in India.
alliance: INDIA Alliance (varies by election and state)
achievements: Contributed to the Indian labour movement.
Advocated land reforms and agrarian rights.
Promoted public education and public healthcare.
Supported expansion of workers' rights and trade unions.
Participated in coalition governments at the state level.
Played an active role in parliamentary debates on social welfare.
criticisms: Critics argue that the party's electoral influence has declined over time.
Political opponents have criticised some of its economic policies.
The party has faced challenges expanding beyond its traditional support base.
Analysts have noted reduced parliamentary representation in recent years.
protests: Farmer protests and agricultural reform campaigns.
Protests regarding privatisation of public sector enterprises.
Campaigns on inflation, unemployment and public welfare.
majorSchemes: Support for Universal Public Distribution System
timeline: 1930s - Participation in labour and peasant movements.
1957 - CPI supported India's first democratically elected communist government in Kerala.
1964 - Split leading to the formation of CPI(M).
2004 - Supported the UPA Government from outside.
2024 - Contested Lok Sabha elections as part of opposition alliances in several states.

statesGoverned.status: Part of Left Democratic Front governments

faqs.question: When was CPI founded?
faqs.answer: The Communist Party of India was founded on 26 December 1925.

faqs.question: Who is the current General Secretary?
What ideology does CPI follow?
faqs.answer: Communism, Marxism-Leninism, democratic socialism, secularism and social justice.

faqs.question: Which states have had a significant CPI presence?
faqs.answer: Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Bihar, Andhra Pradesh and several other states through alliances and legislative representation.
